hints: The period of the sine function $\sin(a(x+b))$ is $\frac{2\pi}{a}$. From the graph, the period is $4\pi$, so $a = \frac{1}{2}$.
Determine the horizontal phase shift $b$: with $a = \frac{1}{2}$, one possible value is $b = \frac{\pi}{3}$.
walkthrough:
Determine the parameter $a$ from the period of the curve:
$$\text{Period} = 4\pi \implies \frac{2\pi}{a} = 4\pi \implies a = \frac{1}{2}$$

Determine a possible value for the phase constant $b$:
$$b = \frac{\pi}{3} \quad \left(\text{or } \frac{\pi}{3} + 4n\pi \text{ for } n \in \mathbb{Z}\right)$$

ai_rubric.Graphs of Trigonometric Functions: Identifies $a = \frac{1}{2}$ and one valid value such as $b = \frac{\pi}{3}$.

hints: Apply the horizontal transformation to the $x$-coordinate of the stationary point to get $4p - 8$ (or $4(p-2)$).
Apply the vertical transformation to the $y$-coordinate to get $-3q$.
walkthrough:
Determine the transformed $x$-coordinate in terms of $p$:
$$x = 4p - 8 \quad \text{or} \quad 4(p - 2)$$

Determine the transformed $y$-coordinate in terms of $q$:
$$y = -3q$$

State the coordinates of the stationary point of the transformed curve:
$$(4p - 8, -3q) \quad \text{or} \quad (4(p - 2), -3q)$$
